otsu_calibration_note: Grid-searched (40 data-driven t candidates x 7 a_limit fractions, precision>=0.8 constraint, ranked by F1) against 51472 frames (14448 positive) sampled from the full corpus the same way FireSVMDetector full-corpus training is sampled (waveshare fire-train scenes in full + 1500/camera/session from every synth room). IMPORTANT finding: the unconstrained F1-optimum (no precision floor) degenerates to predicting fire on nearly every frame (t_ign=30.1, precision=28%, recall=98%, accuracy=29%) because F1 never penalizes false positives via tn -- rejected as operationally useless (see reports/otsu_threshold_calibration.json for the full grid and both configs). t_fire and a_limit are empirically INERT across their whole tested range at the validated t_ign -- every genuine hot blob found on this corpus is small (<0.5% of frame), so the two-tier ignition/potential-fire design barely engages its second branch here; both are kept at their original documented values (60.0 C, ~3% of frame) since the data does not argue for changing them. Held-out numbers below are on the same fire_test_scenes FireSVMDetector is evaluated against.
